name: Varwof PKI Core
description: Varwof PKI core engine operation permissions
author: varwof

capabilities.usage: Used when initializing a new PKI hierarchy, establishing a new trust root, or issuing a sub-CA. A one-time initialization operation; re-authorization is usually not needed after creation.
capabilities.when_not: Not needed for routine certificate issuance/query tasks; only needed when an operations administrator initializes the PKI.

capabilities.usage: Used to permanently remove a CA that is no longer in use along with its associated configuration. A dangerous operation, typically restricted to superadmins.
capabilities.when_not: Must never be granted for routine issuance/query tasks; deletion affects the entire trust chain.

capabilities.usage: Used to see which CAs exist in the system (browsing the PKI structure, selecting an issuance target).
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; a read-only capability that can be a base grant for most roles.

capabilities.summary: View detailed information for a single CA
capabilities.usage: Used to view a CA's certificate, validity, status, and other details.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; a read-only capability.
examples: Check a CA certificate's validity period

ca_scope.description: Scope of sub-CAs that can be issued (restricts the sub-CA scope)

capabilities.usage: Used to extend the PKI hierarchy and create sub-CAs for independent business domains.
capabilities.when_not: Routine certificate issuance (cert:issue) does not need this capability; only needed when creating a new CA tier.
examples: Create an independent sub-CA for a department

ca_scope.description: List of CAs allowed for issuance (restricts sub-CA issuance scope)

capabilities.usage: Used to issue new certificates for services, devices, users, or agents. The most common certificate operation.
capabilities.when_not: Pure query tasks (list/info) do not need it; existing certificates should be renewed with cert:renew rather than re-issued.
examples: Issue a certificate for an HTTPS service
Issue an AIC certificate for an AI agent

ca_scope.description: List of CAs where revocation is allowed

capabilities.usage: Used when a private key is compromised, the subject is no longer legitimate, or a certificate is reclaimed after task completion.
capabilities.when_not: Read-only tasks do not need it; revocation is a sensitive operation that should be limited to the smallest scope.
examples: Revoke a certificate after a private key leak
Revoke a temporary certificate after an agent task completes

capabilities.usage: Used when a certificate is about to expire and the same subject must continue operating. Typically keeps the original public key or regenerates it.
capabilities.when_not: First-time access by a new subject should use cert:issue; expiration reclamation should use cert:revoke.
examples: Renew an agent certificate on expiry

capabilities.summary: Query the certificate list (filterable by CA/status/subject)
capabilities.usage: Used to search issued certificates and check their status (valid/revoked/expired). A read-only capability.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; a read-only capability that can be a base grant.
examples: List all certificates under a CA
Look up a certificate's revocation status

capabilities.usage: Used to download certificate files, hand them to a peer, or back them up. A read-only capability.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions, but note that the export is a public certificate, not a private key.
examples: Export a service certificate for an Nginx config
Download a certificate for client deployment

capabilities.summary: Issue multiple certificates in a batch
capabilities.usage: Used to issue certificates for a large number of devices/services at once (bulk onboarding, bulk expansion).
capabilities.when_not: Use cert:issue for single certificates; no batch permission needed.

capabilities.usage: Used to generate/update a CRL for client validation after a revocation.
capabilities.when_not: Pure query tasks do not need it; usually triggered automatically by the revocation flow.
examples: Generate the latest CRL after revocation

capabilities.usage: Used by clients to check certificate revocation status or for audit inspection. A read-only capability.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.
examples: Check whether a CRL contains a certificate

capabilities.usage: Used when providing an OCSP online revocation status query service. Usually held by the core service itself.
capabilities.when_not: Ordinary agent/user tasks do not need this capability.

capabilities.usage: Used to manage PKI user identities and assign role permissions. A sensitive administrative operation.
capabilities.when_not: Ordinary certificate operations do not need user management permissions.
examples: Assign a role to a user

capabilities.usage: Used to view system users and confirm identities. A read-only capability.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.description: Revoke all of a user's certificates
capabilities.summary: Revoke all certificates of a user
capabilities.usage: Used to revoke all certificates of a user on departure or account compromise.
capabilities.when_not: Use cert:revoke to revoke a single certificate.
examples: Revoke all of a user's certificates after departure

capabilities.usage: Used to view operation records or troubleshoot. A read-only capability.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to hand logs to a SIEM, for offline archival, or compliance audits.
capabilities.when_not: Use log:read for viewing only.
examples: Export the last 30 days of logs to an audit system

capabilities.usage: Used to view statistics such as issuance and revocation counts. Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to download report data (CSV/JSON).
capabilities.when_not: Use report:view for on-page viewing only.
examples: Export a report to a finance system

capabilities.usage: Used to generate reports on custom criteria.
capabilities.when_not: Use report:view for preset reports only.
examples: Generate an issuance report for a custom time range

capabilities.usage: Used to view the current configuration (listen ports, CA paths, etc.). Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to change configuration and hot-reload. A sensitive operation; changes may affect all services.
capabilities.when_not: Must never be granted for routine tasks; only needed by operations administrators.

capabilities.usage: Used to approve pending certificate requests (manual review flow).
capabilities.when_not: Fully automated issuance does not need RA approval.

capabilities.usage: Used to reject non-compliant certificate requests.
capabilities.when_not: Same as ra:approve; only needed by approvers.

capabilities.usage: Used to establish a trust bridge between two PKI domains. An advanced PKI operation.
capabilities.when_not: Not needed for issuance within a single domain.
examples: Mutual trust between two enterprise PKIs

capabilities.usage: Used to revoke a cross-domain trust bridge.
capabilities.when_not: Not needed for single-domain operations.

capabilities.usage: Used to configure certificate event notifications (issued/revoked/expiring) to external systems.
capabilities.when_not: Tasks that do not subscribe to notifications do not need it.
examples: Configure a certificate expiry reminder webhook

capabilities.usage: Used to recover a private key from escrow. An extremely sensitive operation.
capabilities.when_not: Must never be granted for routine tasks; only for authorized key-escrow administrators.
examples: Recover a lost service private key

capabilities.summary: Manage DNS records (domain validation before certificate issuance)
capabilities.usage: Used to create DNS validation records for certificate issuance (ACME challenges, etc.).
capabilities.when_not: Issuance that does not involve domain validation does not need it.

capabilities.summary: Import a trust anchor / root certificate
capabilities.usage: Used when trusting a new external CA.
capabilities.when_not: Tasks that do not involve external trust do not need it.

capabilities.usage: Used to see which external CAs are currently trusted. Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to revoke trust in an external CA.
capabilities.when_not: Not needed when not managing external trust.

capabilities.usage: Used to manage AI agent identities and sessions connecting to the gateway.
capabilities.when_not: An agent executing its own tasks does not need to manage other agents.

capabilities.usage: Used to browse the API documentation. Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to log in to the web management interface.
capabilities.when_not: Pure API-call tasks do not need it.
examples: Log in to the management console
